title: Claude helped me add cloud saves to my browser based game within minutes
author: dawnfist
selftext:
I started receiving reports from iPhone users that their saves were not carrying over between sessions. Save data was supposed to be stored in the browser/history. 

I gave the report to claude. Opus was able to investigate and test the report to confirm the validity and find the cause. 

Apparently, there is a security feature on safari/iphones that prevents cross site tracking. Since itch.io has the game page as one url but loads the game within the page from another url, iphones with this setting turned on could not carry over saves.

Claude offered a few options to resolve. Export saves, trying running the game in a new tab. New tab didn't work. itch.io didnt give the user the option to do so on mobile.

So I decided to kill two birds with one stone. Set up cloud saves. This would prevent data loss as well as allow users to hop between devices and continue their game.

I already had a cloudflare account that I set up so the game could have a webpage for the wiki.

I asked claude how to get cloud saves set up while game was hosted on itch.io.

It gave me a step by step break down. Walked me through each phase of clicking here and copy pasting links there. Then I gave it the worker address and client ID from itch.io (both public info) and it was able to implement the cloud save process in the game.

Now users get a prompt at title screen that allows them to choose to sign in with itch.io account or just store saves locally.

I added a privacy notice on my game page and gave people a way to contact me if they want data deleted (only username and game data are stored). And that's that.

I'd say all told maybe a half hour of work and players get a new feature and save security.

I was excited about this development and decided to share in case anyone else was concerned about how difficult cloud saves might be to implement.
